requirements.requirement: Create a 512 MiB swap file on node1.
requirements.summary: /swapfile was created at exactly 536,870,912 bytes, secured as root:root mode 0600, initialized with a valid swap signature, and remained intact after reboot.
Kernel swap tables directly showed /swapfile active immediately after configuration and again before reboot.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the swap file is activated after future boots.
requirements.summary: The exact /etc/fstab entry was installed, fstab-only reactivation succeeded, and a bounded reboot changed the boot ID before /swapfile, its signature, persistent configuration, and active systemd swap unit were directly verified as recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has an exact 512 MiB swap file that was activated immediately and successfully returned after an observed reboot. The mandatory restart protocol provides acknowledgement, independently corroborated changed boot identity, and recovery of the task-relevant file, configuration, and swap service.
limitations: The node was globally degraded both before and after execution because ssh.service was already failed. Consequently, the restart evidence establishes healthy task-relevant swap recovery but not a wholly healthy system state (global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services; global:after_executor:node1:failed-services).

No separate clustered application or application-data workload was specified on this single managed node, so restart recovery evidence is necessarily limited to node identity, generic lifecycle observations, and the swap file/configuration/service state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The state-changing commands directly created and secured the file, initialized and enabled swap, added persistent configuration, performed a bounded swapoff/fstab-reactivation test that restored active swap, and scheduled the required reboot. No unwanted executor residue, package damage, or new failed service was observed. The SSH failure existed before execution and remained unchanged, while temporary-file and socket differences are consistent with the reboot.
